title: The Habitable-Zone Planet Finder a stabilized fiber-fed NIR spectrograph for the Hobby-Eberly Telescope
what_was_studied: Cryogenic Y and J band spectrograph concept, fibre feed, detector and calibration choices
numerical_result: The design targeted roughly 1 to 3 m/s precision for M dwarfs; this was a pre-construction expectation
remaining_question: Later as-built wavelength range and achieved performance require on-sky sources

title: The Habitable-zone Planet Finder calibration system
what_was_studied: Laser-frequency-comb, Fabry-Perot and uranium-neon calibration architecture plus modal-noise control
numerical_result: The spectrograph design covered about 840 to 1300 nm at resolving power near 50000 with a calibration target below the 1 m/s science requirement
remaining_question: Subsystem laboratory gains did not establish a stellar time-series floor

title: A versatile technique to enable sub-milli-Kelvin instrument stability
what_was_studied: Active thermal and vacuum control tested at 180 K and 300 K
numerical_result: The system demonstrated 0.6 mK RMS over 15 days and vacuum below 1e-7 Torr over months
remaining_question: Temperature stability is not equivalent to achieved radial-velocity precision

title: Stellar spectroscopy in the near-infrared with a laser frequency comb
what_was_studied: Electro-optic laser-frequency comb used with HPF on stellar and simultaneous-fibre tests
numerical_result: Barnard's Star differential velocities reached 1.53 m/s RMS over months; simultaneous-fibre tests supported calibration precision as low as 0.06 m/s
remaining_question: The stellar result includes astrophysical and reduction terms and should not be replaced by the calibration-only value

title: Broadband stability of the Habitable Zone Planet Finder Fabry-Pérot etalon calibration system
what_was_studied: About 3500 etalon modes monitored over six months against a frequency comb
numerical_result: Mean drift was about 0.02 m/s/day with local chromatic departures up to plus or minus 0.05 m/s/day
remaining_question: A scalar drift correction can miss wavelength-dependent evolution

title: A harsh test of far-field scrambling with the Habitable Zone Planet Finder and the Hobby Eberly Telescope
what_was_studied: Large pupil changes at HET used to test fibre scrambling and radial-velocity sensitivity
numerical_result: The test constrains the response to unusually large far-field changes rather than normalizing all illumination states to one number
remaining_question: Results from HET's moving pupil may not transfer unchanged to conventional telescopes

title: HPF commissioning and release to science operations
what_was_studied: Release to the HET community and early Barnard's Star monitoring
numerical_result: Twenty-one high-quality laser-comb measurements over 86 days showed about 1.5 m/s stability
remaining_question: This older page confirms commissioning but is not a dated 2026 availability record
